samples.summary: New Apply guard compares href *values* against the caret, not link identity, and ignores the selection — so it still lets Apply mutate content the user never opened
samples.evidence: The guard is `editingHref !== null && editor.getLinkAtCursor() !== editingHref` (docs-link-popover.tsx:169). Two bypasses of its own stated purpose ("a silent edit to a link the user never opened"): (1) value, not identity — with two hyperlinks sharing one href, clicking into the second passes the comparison and `insertLink` rewrites that other run via the caret branch (`editor.ts:3646`); (2) it consults only `getLinkAtCursor()` (cursor position), while `insertLink` prefers the *selection* branch (`editor.ts:3582`). Attacker/user path: with the popover open in edit mode, drag-select backwards so the drag ends inside the opened link — focus/caret is inside the link so the guard passes, but the range is wider than the link, `linkRunCoveringRange` declines (`editor.ts:3612`), and `doc.applyInlineStyle(range, {href:url})` at `editor.ts:3634` links the entire dragged span, including text outside the link the popover was opened for. Impact is document-integrity in a shared CRDT doc, not privilege escalation, hence minor; the added guard reads as covering this and does not.

samples.summary: `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` writes an href (and the display text) with no scheme validation; the only sanitizer is the frontend popover, so any other caller of `insertLink` stores an unvalidated href
samples.evidence: `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` applies `{ href: url }` (link-run.ts:103,110) and inserts `url` as document text (link-run.ts:108) without `isSafeUrl`/`hasUrlAlteringChars`. Neither `editor.insertLink` (editor.ts:3576) nor `textBox.insertLink` (text-box-editor.ts:1186) validates either; the single validating caller is `normalizeLinkUrl` in the frontend popover (docs-link-popover.tsx:163). The slides package re-exports the same API unvalidated (`packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:634`), so a link UI added there — or any programmatic holder of `EditorAPI` — stores e.g. `javascript:`/`data:` hrefs into the CRDT. Not exploitable today because I confirmed every read sink is gated (`text-editor.ts:1822`, `text-editor.ts:2176`, `docs-link-popover.tsx:217/224`, `serialize/markdown.ts:382`, `export/pdf-painter.ts:903`), so this is defense-in-depth: validation should sit at the store boundary rather than only in one UI. Searched: grep for `isSafeUrl|hasUrlAlteringChars|normalizeLinkUrl` repo-wide, grep for `insertLink(` across frontend/docs/slides src, and read `store/read-only.ts` plus `MUTATING_METHODS`.

samples.summary: Pasted HTML `<a href>` is stored verbatim with no protocol allowlist, so document state can already hold `javascript:`/`data:` hrefs that the link-edit paths touched here operate on
samples.evidence: `parseHtmlToBlocks` copies the raw attribute into the inline style (`clipboard.ts:610-613`, and again at `clipboard.ts:712-715`), and the clipboard JSON reader does the same (`clipboard.ts:148-149`), with no `isSafeUrl` gate. Vector: paste HTML containing `x` into a doc; the unsafe href persists in the shared document and is what the popover/link-run code (including the new `linkTextFollowsHref` comparison) reasons about. I could not complete an exploit chain: every render/activate sink I checked re-gates on `isSafeUrl` (`text-editor.ts:1822`, `text-editor.ts:2176`, `docs-link-popover.tsx:217`), and both exporters gate, so this is unsanitized-at-rest rather than an XSS today. Pre-existing and outside the diff; raised because this change adds new code that trusts stored hrefs. Searched: grep for `href` in packages/docs/src (all 11 files), read clipboard.ts href sites, markdown.ts and pdf-painter.ts gates, and grepped frontend/src/app/docs for `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`.href` sinks.
